newsitem.title: UK: British life insurers warned in ratings report.
newsitem.headline: British life insurers warned in ratings report.

text.p: Some British life insurance companies are pursuing non-profitable new business as they attempt to grab market share and push prices below the reach of smaller competitors, according to a report released by credit rating agency Moody's Investors Service on Monday.

"New business may not be profitable business," Moody's said in a summary of the 88-page report, adding that some insurers were pursuing market share strategies "with the aim of pushing prices below the reach of smaller providers that lack economies of scale needed to achieve lower costs".

Moody's said mutually-owned companies were likely to need stronger partners if they are to compete effectively. It said further consolidation in the sector and a shedding of mutual status was also expected.

The report said that while "well-positioned UK life insurers will continue to be highly rated", downward pressure "will be exerted by the continued high level of competition". Since its last annual outlook, there had been two positive developments in the industry, Moody's said.
It said there had been a significant upturn in new business sales since the third quarter of 1995, and investment markets had strengthened over the last two years.
But it warned that better performing markets were not a "panacea for the industry's ills" adding that a sustained bear market would hit insurers' capitalisation.

Moody's said the industry also faces medium-term challenges which include heightened competition, both internally and from outside, the need to cut costs and pressure to consolidate as well as difficulty in generating capital.

A poor image of the industry and its products and a period of lower investment returns will also contribute to a downward pressure on ratings. "The industry survivors will continue to be cost-effective in the post disclosure' era in which most costs are transparent to the consumer," Moody's said.
While multi-distribution of life products has been difficult to achieve, Moody's said that "more limited channels can be effective if properly focused and resourced".
